excerpt: Inspect a Dubai apartment before handover with a room-by-room snagging checklist and a clear process for documenting and following up defects.
introduction:
A snagging inspection records issues in an apartment before or around handover so the buyer and developer can agree the next steps. Check the actual unit against the signed plan and specification, photograph issues with permission and ask how each will be acknowledged and resolved. The contract and applicable law determine responsibilities; an inspection list alone does not do so.

This checklist is practical guidance, not a replacement for a qualified technical inspection. Do not dismantle equipment or test electrical systems unless you are authorised and competent to do so.
takeaways: Bring the signed plan and specification, and record each defect by room and exact location.
Inspect finishes, windows, plumbing, cooling and safely accessible fittings; use a specialist for technical concerns.
Agree the reporting, acknowledgement and reinspection process in writing and retain the complete record.

sections.heading: Prepare before the inspection
sections.body:
Confirm the unit number, appointment, access arrangements and whether an independent inspector may attend. Bring the signed floor plan and specification, a checklist, a phone or camera and a way to record measurements. Ask whether electricity, water and cooling will be available for appropriate tests.

Read the handover notice and agreement's process for defects, acceptance and follow-up. If an item or remedy is unclear, seek qualified advice before signing a document you do not understand. The [Dubai off-plan handover checklist](/journal/dubai-off-plan-handover-checklist-for-buyers) covers the payment and registration steps around the inspection.

DLD's [project status service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/) provides project information; match the project and developer to your documents.

table.caption: Room-by-room snagging checklist
rows: Finish, visible cracks, tiles and skirting
Cabinets, fittings, visible leaks and drainage
Visible controls and safely accessible operation
Finish, drainage, safety and allocated parking

sections.heading: Inspect finishes, doors and windows
sections.body:
Walk through each room in a consistent order. Look for uneven paint, damaged tiles, loose skirting, gaps in finishes and marks that need clarification. Open and close doors and windows where safe; check handles, locks, alignment and visible seals. Note whether the issue affects appearance, operation or safety.

Compare the layout and included items with the contract and approved plan. Measure spaces important to your use, but ask a qualified professional how any area discrepancy should be assessed. A marketing image may not be the contractual specification.

Take a wide photograph showing the room and a closer one of the issue. Give each item a number so the developer's response and later reinspection can be matched to the original record.

sections.heading: Check water, cooling and accessible fittings
sections.body:
With permission and services connected, run taps and check visible joints, water pressure and drainage. Look for moisture around sinks, bathrooms and accessible plumbing. Ask about hot water operation and whether tests were carried out before your visit. A short observation cannot prove that a system has no hidden defect.

Check the cooling controls and ask for operating instructions, maintenance information and warranty documents. Inspect safely accessible lights and switches without opening electrical panels or handling exposed wiring. Arrange a qualified specialist if operation is abnormal or a safety issue is suspected.

For appliances, record the model, visible condition and any operating test permitted by the developer. Confirm which items are included and when their warranties begin under the relevant terms.

sections.heading: Record and follow up each snag
sections.body:
Use a simple record: item number, room, description, photograph, date, response and reinspection outcome. Ask the developer to acknowledge the list and explain the repair process and expected update dates. Record whether an item was resolved or needs further review; do not mark it complete solely because a repair was scheduled.

If specialist work is needed, request a written assessment and obtain qualified advice about responsibility under the agreement. DLD's [FAQs](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/frequently-asked-questions) discuss escrow arrangements and retention relating to defects; the applicable contract and current law still need to be checked for your situation.

Keep all correspondence, signed forms and photographs. If there is a disagreement, seek advice about the appropriate official process and deadlines.

sections.heading: Understand possible repair costs
sections.body:
For illustration only, imagine a qualified contractor estimates AED 6,500 for one category of remedial work, AED 2,500 for another and AED 1,000 for a third. The total is AED 10,000. The chart shows example repair estimates to help organise an inspection and handover budget.

Actual responsibility depends on the agreement, applicable law and the facts. Obtain itemised written estimates where useful and confirm who will perform and fund the work. Avoid accepting an allowance or signing away a disputed issue without understanding its effect.

chart.title: Example itemised repair estimates
chart.note: Sample estimates total AED 10,000; payment responsibility is not assumed.

sections.heading: Check outdoor space and access
sections.body:
Where the unit has a balcony or terrace, inspect visible finishes, doors, drainage and railings without leaning over or carrying out unsafe tests. Ask how water drains and report any visible damage. Confirm that access to the space and the position of any equipment match the relevant plan and specification.

Inspect the path from the apartment to the lift and allocated parking where access is permitted. Record a common-area issue separately from a defect inside the unit and ask building management who will handle it. A unit inspection should not imply that an entire building has been technically certified.

sections.heading: Reinspect and retain the handover record
sections.body:
When work is reported complete, revisit the same items and record whether each is resolved. Check that repairs have not caused new damage and note any items that need a further appointment. Confirm keys, access cards, parking, meter readings, manuals and building management contacts as part of the wider handover.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) explains why building management and ongoing costs also matter after purchase. Browse [Aliyas Dubai projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai) or [contact Aliyas](/contact) to discuss the documents to request for a specific property.

Retain the final inspection record, warranties, receipts and registration documents for future maintenance or resale.
